messages.author: a798ae8eb83fb9a2
messages.subject: Spatial moving average process
parts:
Good afternoon.

I would like to ask how to implement the spatial moving average process with the R-INLA library. By the way, does anyone know how to define the covariance matrix in the inla() function by ourselves?

Warm regards,
Xiaojun

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Spatial moving average process
parts:
# Moving average model
I have not done this. I think an inspired use of the copy functionality will be able to. Does anyone else know?

# Define the covariance matrix: Yes!
We use inverse covariance matrices, as these are often sparse. (Precision matrix)
inla.doc('generic0')
inla.doc('generic1')
inla.doc('generic2')
inla.doc('generic3') ?

And for full generality, there is Rgeneric, which can handle any precision matrix parametrised by a set of hyperparameters.
inla.doc('rgeneric')
demo(rgeneric)

Kind regards,
Haakon Bakka
